rationale: CrystalMk is a small (7 functions, ~5KB text) dense numeric kernel dominated by hot loops in Crystal_Cholesky, Crystal_div, and Crystal_pow, so instruction substitution (SUB) is favored strongly as the primary transformation since it adds arithmetic-level opacity with negligible runtime and size cost and minimal correctness risk on these loops; BCF and FLA get moderate weights because their bogus-control-flow and dispatch overhead would tax the tight inner loops of Cholesky/div/pow, so they are encouraged mainly for the larger, less loop-dominant functions like SPEdriver and main; SPLIT is kept cheap and moderately weighted to diversify block structure at almost no cost; IBR is mid-weighted since indirect branching helps confuse static control-flow recovery but adds branch-dispatch cost in hot code; IGV is moderately weighted because init/main/SPEdriver share global state worth hiding; ICALL is omitted entirely because with only 7 mostly-inlined numeric functions there are few call sites to protect, so indirect-call rewriting would add vtable-style overhead and correctness risk with almost no diversity gain.
